whenToUse: Each option needs a description, which is hard to fit in a dropdown.
Places where the list can always be visible, such as settings.
People scan quickly with the keyboard to choose.
whenNotToUse: There are two to five options inside a form (a radio group is more familiar).
The list is so long people need to search it (use a combobox).
accessibility: As a WAI-ARIA listbox, the whole list is one Tab stop, and aria-activedescendant announces the current option.
Moving with ↑/↓ and Home/End carries the selection along.
Pressing a letter jumps to the option starting with it.
The selected option shows with both a background color and a check mark.
